description: Displayed in the main hangar painted as Gulf Aviation Dakota G-AMZZ, which is a false identity. True identity per ruudleeuw.com and the lgarey RAF Sharjah page: C-47A c/n 12254, delivered to the USAAF 31 Jan 1944 as 42-92452, to the RAF as FZ669, to the RCAF 1946, civil as C-GCXE (1976), HH-CMG, HI-502 and N688EA (1993); arrived at Sharjah marked G-DJKP and was repainted as G-AMZZ. The real G-AMZZ (c/n 33340/KN648) was stored at Bahrain and presumed scrapped. Photographed at the museum 18 Sep 2013 (ABPic) and reported in place in 2019-2024 visitor accounts. Museum reported temporarily closed for renovation from late 2024 through at least June 2025 (glimpsesofuae.com Oct 2024, Wikipedia Mahatta Fort June 2025); reopening date not found.
aliases: C47A; DC-3; DC3; Dakota; G-AMZZ; G-DJKP; FZ669; N688EA; C-GCXE; HI-502; HH-CMG; 12254; C47; HI502

description: Painted in Gulf Aviation colours as Anson G-AKVW, a false identity. True identity Anson C.19 TX183, c/n 33756, built Yeadon 1946 (lgarey page; Alan Wilson Flickr caption 14 Sep 2015 and airhistory.net photo 12 Apr 2005 both state painted as G-AKVW but is in fact ex G-BSMF / TX183). Formerly with the Shuttleworth Collection, restoration to fly begun at Duxford in the 1980s but never completed, civil registration G-BSMF. Displayed in the main hangar; photographed by ABPic 18 Sep 2013. Museum temporarily closed for renovation late 2024 to at least mid-2025.

description: Painted in Gulf Aviation colours as Heron G-ANFE, a false identity. Per the lgarey RAF Sharjah page: c/n 14072, delivered 1955 to West African Airways as VR-NAQ, to Overseas Aviation as G-ARKU (1961), converted to Royal Navy Sea Heron C.20 XR443, later VH-NJP with Heron Airlines in Australia; acquired for the museum in 2003 and repainted as G-ANFE. ABPic photo 18 Sep 2013 lists it as Sea Heron C.20 VH-NJP. Wikipedia gives c/n 14034, which conflicts with lgarey; c/n not settled. Museum temporarily closed for renovation late 2024 to at least mid-2025.

description: Auster J/1 Autocrat G-AJRE, genuine registration. Dismantled at Coventry, shipped to Sharjah, reassembled and flown around the UAE, landing at the museum on 5 Oct 2012 for the 80th anniversary of the first landing at Sharjah (PPRuNe RAF Sharjah thread; lgarey page). Photographed at the museum 18 Sep 2013 (ABPic). Museum temporarily closed for renovation late 2024 to at least mid-2025.

Forward fuselage / nose section only. Built as Comet 2 c/n 06023, first production Comet 2, first flown 27 Aug 1953 as BOAC G-AMXA; to the RAF 1958 as XK655 and converted to Comet R.2 ELINT aircraft for 51 Squadron, which frequently staged through Sharjah. Static at Strathallan from Aug 1974, airframe scrapped c.1990 with only the nose surviving (aerialvisuals dossier 114418); nose later displayed at Gatwick before going to Sharjah. Photographed at the museum 18 Sep 2013 (ABPic). Displayed wearing BOAC marks G-AMXA. Museum temporarily closed for renovation late 2024 to at least mid-2025.

description: Forward fuselage only, painted in Gulf Air colours. Super VC10 c/n 883, first flight 19 Apr 1969, delivered to East African Airways 30 Apr 1969 as 5X-UVJ (Uganda register); to the RAF, converted to K.3 tanker and delivered to 101 Squadron as ZA149 on 14 May 1985; final flight to Bruntingthorpe Mar 2013. Forward fuselage converted to Gulf Air scheme and interior, left Bruntingthorpe 23 Mar 2016, unloaded at Khor Fakkan 30 Apr 2016 and installed at the museum by 26 May 2016 (vc10.net; The National 7 Nov 2016). Photographed 22 Jan 2020 (Flickr, Michael Kelly). airportspotting.com gives c/n 884, vc10.net detailed page gives 883. Museum temporarily closed for renovation late 2024 to at least mid-2025.
aliases: Super VC10; VC-10; VC10 K3; 5X-UVJ; ZA149; 883; nose section; VC10
